research_gap.description: Large Language Models exhibit a significant disparity between answer accuracy and reasoning faithfulness, often arriving at correct answers through factually incorrect intermediate steps.

research_gap.description: A lack of fine-grained, automated tools exists to systematically assess the truthfulness of corporate environmental claims and distinguish actionable implementation from vague greenwashing.
citations: \citep{Towards Robust ESG Analysis Against Greenwashing Risks: Aspect-Action Analysis with Cross-Category Generalization}

problem_statement.statement: LLMs suffer from hallucinations that undermine trust in high-stakes financial and political tasks, such as ESG analysis where corporate narratives often prioritize symbolic legitimation (green talk) over substantive commitment (green walk). Current analytical frameworks lack the structured reasoning capabilities to reliably separate these performative claims from actionable steps, leading to inaccurate sustainability assessments and low-resource policy detection failures.
citations: \citep{Direct evaluation of chain-of-thought in multi-hop reasoning with knowledge graphs}
\citep{Critical Discourse Analysis in Corporate Reports: Legitimation Strategies in the Context of Environmental Controversies}
\citep{The harm of symbolic actions and green-washing: Corporate actions and communications on environmental performance and their financial implications}
\citep{Towards Robust ESG Analysis Against Greenwashing Risks: Aspect-Action Analysis with Cross-Category Generalization}

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: The ratio of correctly predicted observations to the total observations in sustainability and political tasks.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate a higher proportion of correct classification and reasoning paths.

metrics.name: F1-Score
metrics.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall used to evaluate overall performance in hallucination detection and stance classification.
metrics.interpretation: A higher F1 score indicates a better balance between finding all correct cases and avoiding false positives.

metrics.name: ESG-action orientation
metrics.definition: The proportion of topic terms focused specifically on concrete ESG actions rather than vague sentiment.
metrics.formula: Action Orientation = Count of Action-Focused Terms / Total Count of Topic Terms
metrics.interpretation: Higher percentages indicate disclosures with greater material significance and concrete implementation.

metrics.name: Specificity
metrics.definition: The proportion of actual negatives that are correctly identified by the hallucination detection framework.
metrics.interpretation: Indicates the model's ability to avoid falsely labeling factual information as hallucinations.

metrics.name: Maj@8
metrics.definition: A consistency metric calculating the accuracy of the majority solution among eight sampled reasoning paths.
metrics.interpretation: Measures the robustness of the model's self-consistency in logic-heavy reasoning tasks.
